title: Determination 2014/017: three schist wall-cladding systems proposed for future houses, Queenstown and Arrowtown
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE determination under the Building Act 2004); comparative test only, not Alberta; NZ code references retained as written
code_edition: Building Code (Schedule 1, Building Regulations 1992), as cited; clauses B1, B2, E2
document_date: 8 April 2014 (page-header date; signature date not captured)

facts.text: The applicant is the licensed building practitioner who designed existing and proposed houses; the authority is Queenstown Lakes District Council.

The authority had issued consents and code compliance certificates for existing houses with similar schist wall cladding, and the reason for the application is the authority's proposed refusal of a further consent.
No documentation for specific building work was supplied; the cladding systems are considered on a general basis, and Clause B1 compliance will rely on engineering design at building-consent stage.
Type 1 (timber-framed): drainage sheets and fibre-cement backing fixed through 20 mm H3 cavity battens and building wrap, with stonework tied by engineered galvanised steel ties.

Type 2 (insulated concrete block): bituminous damp-proof membrane, 50 x 50 mm H3.2 battens at 600 mm centres, drainage sheets and EPS insulation, with stonework tied by engineered ties. Type 3 (uninsulated concrete block) uses a liquid bituminous membrane and drainage sheets.
Other houses (a 2004 garage/sleepout, a 2010 house, a 2013 house and a 2014 design) informed the analysis but are outside the matter to be determined.
